tickerText: [TENNIS] Team Europe leads Team World 7-5 after Laver Cup Day 2 at London's O2 as Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points to beat Taylor Fritz 6-3, 4-6, 13-11, while Alex de Minaur stunned Alexander Zverev 2-6, 7-6(5), 11-9 and Learner Tien beat Flavio Cobolli — Sunday's matches are worth three points each in the race to 13 • [SQUASH] India's Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh play for Asian Games gold on Sept. 27 in Nagoya against Malaysia's Sivasangari Subramaniam and Ng Eain Yow, with singles titles also carrying LA28 Olympic qualification • [BADMINTON] Five Indonesian quarterfinalists headline Sept. 27 action in Ichinomiya as Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan beat Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand 21-18, 21-9 to reach the women's doubles semis and clinch Malaysia's first women's doubles medal since 2014 • [PICKLEBALL] The Carvana PPA Tour's 1,000-point Rate Las Vegas Open opens Sept. 28 at the Darling Tennis Center with Anna Leigh Waters two titles shy of 200 after Mesa and pro TV coverage from Oct. 1 • [TABLE TENNIS] Men's doubles semifinals and women's singles semifinals run Sept. 27 at Sky Hall Toyota while India's campaign closed with one mixed doubles bronze after Manush Shah and Yashaswini Ghorpade exited in singles pre-quarters

newsItems.title: Europe Leads at Laver Cup
newsItems.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz edged Taylor Fritz 6-3, 4-6, 13-11 after saving two match points on Sept. 26, and Team Europe finished Laver Cup Day 2 with a 7-5 lead over Team World heading into Sunday's triple-point matches in London.

newsItems.title: India's Squash Gold Day
newsItems.excerpt: Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh both reached Asian Games singles finals on Sept. 27 in Nagoya, each one win from India's first individual squash gold and a direct LA28 Olympic berth as squash debuts in Los Angeles.

newsItems.title: Waters Eyes 200 in Vegas
newsItems.excerpt: Anna Leigh Waters arrives at the Rate Las Vegas Open on 198 career PPA Tour titles after winning singles and mixed doubles in Mesa, with the 1,000-point event running Sept. 28–Oct. 4 at the Darling Tennis Center.

newsItems.title: India's TT Ends at Asiad
newsItems.excerpt: Manush Shah and Yashaswini Ghorpade lost in singles pre-quarterfinals on Sept. 26, leaving India with one Asian Games table tennis medal — bronze for Shah and Diya Chitale in mixed doubles — as semifinals continue Sept. 27.
